items.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: So eventually James Chirillo and Mark Lopeman and Mike Christiansen arranged

ctx.x: I was gone. My place was taken by Ted Nash. And I’ll say now, you know, thirty-five years, thirty-four years retrospect, Ted’s a better section player than I am you know. But that was a life lesson, you know what I mean? And then Benny died the following June and I mean I kept doing gigs with the band anyway, when I had gigs, and Benny passed away and then I decided soon after there that this was not going to be a Benny Goodman ghost band. I mean (a) his estate eventually said there will be no ghost band. But I…

that many who you’d want to hear play a Benny Goodman concert, because it would suck. I mean there are a handful, but not that many. And I didn’t know them you know. So I gave that up and then started recording our own albums and we did four or five albums for MusicMasters. And they were nice combinations of, I mean I’m no great arranger. I can arrange — the most arranging I ever did was for Bobby Short during the years when I had his band. But with my own big band, no. I mean I wanted much better writers than…
Well you are one of the luckiest guys in the world then.

items.title: James Chirillo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: And so Loren called me and I did it

ctx.x: Well Loren Schoenberg was working for Benny at that time. He was sort of like his secretary, and, you know, fielding phone calls, doing things, whatever. But Loren had had his own — pardon me — he had his own band, and when, from what I gather, when Benny was approached by PBS to do a PBS special, “Let’s Dance,” he just asked Loren to put the band together, to get a band together. And Loren always had an interest, I mean his primary interest, especially at that time, whenever he would get his band together, would…

Benny had heard that band and says, “Get that band together.” I was pretty new in town, Loren knew me though. And I gather for the first rehearsal Howard Alden did the first rehearsal, and he was playing in that band at that time, but he couldn’t make the next one. And so Loren called me and I did it, and I don’t know if — for whatever reason — either Benny said let him go or Loren said you know I want to use this guy, but who knows, but I ended up doing it. So there you go. Yeah Benny. I mean everybody hears…
